full_judgment: 64. PW 15 is Kubaleswar Tripura, Executive Engineer, PWD stationed in Comilla. He went for the measurement and to determine the valuation of the property under memo given by Deputy Director, Zibon Krishna Roy, Anti-Corruption Commission and submitted report on 3-5-2007. The report along with a forwarding and the envelope which is Exhibit 15 series. He took valuation on the basis of schedule of 1992 and the valuation was assessed at Taka 20,02,965. The valuation covered bound-any, road, pucca garage, electricity, water, sewerage and gas. From the valuation overhead charge, VAT and the profit of the contractor was deducted. In his cross-examination he stated that he fixed the age of the building coming to know from the local public and that is on presumption. He admitted that there may be difference in the schedule as to the valuation. He stated that the valuation was taken on the basis of schedule of 1989 in place of 1992. He stated that in the event the schedule was followed applicable for the year 1989 the valuation of the property certainly would have come down. He admitted that the schedule is changeable and it was changed 6/7 times. He stated that there is a branch of Agrani Bank in the said building. He does not know whether the Building is constructed on financial support of Agrani Bank. Some of the organizations may value the property on their own. He did not inquire them was any valuation of the said building by Agrani Bank. He did not take any information about ownership of the building. He did not know as to what kind of cement was used in the building. He stated that the valuation of building may differ on the count of quality of cement. He stated that he does not have the knowledge as to quantity of goods. He did not make survey on that. He does not know as to what kind of iron rods were used in the building. The evidence of PW 15 as to valuation of the aforesaid building also does not have any weight at all, because the PW had no knowledge as to the age of the building and the materials that were used at the time of construction. In the absence of the knowledge as to the age of the building the PW 15 had no means to know when the said building was constructed. Unless the year of construction is known, the perfect rate applicable for the relevant year cannot be determined and such rate so determined is a mere imaginary rate. The Learned Advocate submits that it is imperative to determine the quality of goods for a perfect valuation and that the basic criteria for determining of the rate was fundamentally wrong. Therefore, the assessment so made by PW 15 cannot be of any evidentiary value.
